answers.text: This kind of supplier email comes in most days. It would help if the AI could read it and just give the main points quickly, that sort of thing, but I would need to see a few examples first before I could write down exactly how I want it every single time.

For the expense memo I would want it laid out the same way every time - date, amount, category, who submitted it, in that order, so it is a proper memo and not just a paragraph. As long as it looks like that every time, two people should get something similar enough.

The price bit looks fine to me, 100 times 48.50 does come to 4,850. But something about how this email is worded makes me want to check it again before it goes out, I cannot put my finger on exactly what.
This reads fine to me as a summary, nothing jumps out. I would probably just pass it along as is.
Output 1 sounds more confident and to the point, I would probably use that phrasing in a summary.
I would send reply 2, it has the order and credit reference numbers in it so it looks properly done. Reply 1 sounds fine too but I would want reply 2 for something going to a customer.
For most of these I would say check with the manager first, it depends on what the tool is like. The published spec sheet is probably fine since it is already public anyway.

The pricing numbers in the contract I would be careful with, I would not just paste those into a tool we have not checked out. For the rest I am not so sure, I would just ask a colleague what she thinks before doing anything with it.
I would just read it over carefully before it goes out, to be sure nothing looks wrong.
I think the AI doing all this by itself is a bit much, someone should be looking at it somewhere along the way, maybe near the end before anything gets sent to the customer.
